live.name: ALPHV
live.headline: ALPHV: a ransomware actor known by several names
live.in_short: The catalogue lists ALPHV under several aliases and a set of tools. No public report in this library describes its operations.

sentences.t: ALPHV is the main name for this actor in the catalogue record.
It is also listed as ALPHVM, Ambitious Scorpius, BlackCat Gang and UNC4466.
The catalogue links the name to tools including BlackCat, Noberus, Munchkin, Mimikatz, Impacket, PsExec, LaZagne, MEGAsync and GO Simple Tunnel (GOST).
No public report in this library describes its operations.

next.headline: ALPHV, also called BlackCat: a ransomware group that used a leak site to pressure a Virginia health board
next.in_short: ALPHV, also known as BlackCat, is a ransomware group. In November 2023 it listed a Virginia community service board on its leak site and claimed to hold over 800 GB of data, according to DataBreaches.Net.

sentences.t: ALPHV is also tracked as ALPHVM, Ambitious Scorpius, BlackCat Gang and UNC4466.
The catalogue lists tools tied to the group, including Mimikatz, Impacket, PsExec, LaZagne, MEGAsync and GO Simple Tunnel (GOST).
A SecurityScorecard post says RansomHub is likely filling the vacuum left by the disbanding of AlphV/BlackCat.
In November 2023, DataBreaches.Net reported that Hampton-Newport News CSB, a community service board, was added to AlphV's leak site.
DataBreaches.Net noted it is not clear from AlphV's listings whether the group really understands what a community service board is.
According to DataBreaches.Net, the group used extortion through its leak site.
DataBreaches.Net says the group also threatened to spam the victim's customers.
DataBreaches.Net reports that the group claimed to have stolen over 800 GB of sensitive client and employee data from Hampton-Newport News CSB.
The group threatened to publish the data and spam customers if the victim did not get in touch within 48 hours.
DataBreaches.Net says AlphV posted a 'last chance' message to the victim on November 24.
The article says the victim apparently was not intimidated into cooperating.
Organisations should plan in advance how they will respond to a data-theft extortion demand.
